papers.text: Grant the prize pumpkin the freedom of the town. It has asked very politely.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A ticket museum in the old ticket office. Then a ticket office for it.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Set-up of may-ticket-museum. Other: the old ticket office is on the high street; the Guild wanted its window.

papers.text: Name the 7:02 bus after you, Mayor. It is late too, and also waves.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The clock tower's faces disagree. An inquiry will hear each face.
papers.subject: clocks
papers.biggerStudy: Both faces have spoken. The inquiry now wishes to hear the hands.
papers.note: Other: the face over the high street is the one the Guild opens by.

papers.text: Your signature on every bus ticket, Mayor. Each journey, approved.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay for a sign on the bakery: 7:02 EXPECTED SHORTLY.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the sign goes on a shop wall.

papers.text: Keep the pothole by the shoe shop. It is the 7:02's only stop.
papers.subject: potholes
papers.note: Other: the Guild wants the pothole outside its shoe shop filled.

papers.text: A hat for you, Mayor. The clock tower's is on order. No hurry.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it wants the spotters' bench. It has stood for weeks.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT GIVEN SPOTTERS' BENCH; SPOTTERS STAND
clippings.refuse: HAT STILL STANDING. SPOTTERS SIT DOWN

papers.text: The bean rows hide a third of the 7:02. We want that third back.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Raise the 7:02's profile. A ramp outside the shops should do it.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the ramp goes up outside the shops.

papers.text: Be photographed waiting for the 7:02, Mayor. Bring breakfast.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the spotters wait at the allotment stop, on the growers' patch (the feud).

papers.text: A working group on why tickets are so small. It will report on one.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The report no longer fits. The group asks for a season pass.

papers.text: Unveil the new timetable board, Mayor. Point at a likely time.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the timetable board stands in front of a shop window.

papers.text: Move the prize pumpkin out of Till's Teas. People keep ordering it.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Our window says PAUSE AND ADMIRE. The 7:02 does both. Move the stop.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay to paint PROUDLY ADEQUATE on the bus station. Adequately.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Callback: the motto of the loading card.

papers.text: We will hire the bus station wall. Then a bus. Then the queue.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Open our new window, Mayor. It does not open. Declare it anyway.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Sign to say our windows are windows, Mayor. We will frame it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A committee to word the OPEN sign. Two members favour AJAR.
papers.subject: signage
papers.biggerStudy: OPEN is agreed. The committee asks to begin on CLOSED.

papers.text: A committee to issue nose permits for shop windows. One nose each.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The nose committee asks to cover elbows too. And the odd forehead.

papers.text: A sign: SHOPS. Then MORE SHOPS. Then, at the bus stop, NOT BUSES.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the last sign goes up at the spotters' bus stop.

papers.text: A sweeper for weigh-in days. Sweep one leaf, Mayor, for the camera.
papers.subject: ceremonies
papers.note: Other: a sweeper for weigh-in days reads to the growers as a remark about the weigh-in.

papers.text: A glass roof on the high street. Then glass sides. Then it is a window.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the growers want the rain that falls there.

papers.text: Signs at each end of the high street: THE MAYOR'S. STILL THE MAYOR'S.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Swap the clock tower's face for yours, Mayor. Right twice a day.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: 3 visitors in 4 come for the pumpkin. The fourth is lost. Signs?
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Other: the signs go up in the bus station.

papers.text: Open our compost bins by the bus stop, Mayor. Stand upwind.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Rodney promised our fence to the spotters. And to us, first.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Point the clock tower at the plots. Pumpkins it can see do 30 % better.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The 7:02 may not hoot past the plots. Nor the 7:15. Nor the clock.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for a parade permit. The parade is the pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will pay to rename the bus stop PUMPKIN CORNER. It is not a corner.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We would hire the bus station's parcel scales. Ours are too kind.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Pose with the prize pumpkin, Mayor. Its good side, then yours.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Study the high street pothole. Its soil may be better than ours.
papers.subject: potholes
papers.biggerStudy: The soil is promising. The study now asks for a second pothole.

papers.text: A study of the prize pumpkin's admirers. So far: 312, some twice.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The study is complete. It now asks to count those who looked away.

papers.text: A committee on where the 7:02 should look as it passes our plots.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: Settled: ahead. The committee now asks what it should think.

papers.text: Ask the vegetables what they think of you. 90 % have not objected.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A rain gauge for your desk. It is empty now, but one can hope.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the rain gauge: it wants the prize bed. Your desk is too dry.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S RAIN GAUGE GIVEN PRIZE BED
clippings.refuse: RAIN GAUGE SENT BACK, STILL EMPTY
